findings.problem: پوزیشن is the only occurrence of that word in the entire ur catalogue (measured: 1 hit in 1 file, the new key), while the catalogue's existing name for the same control concept is مقام: ur/ui.chat.attachments.json:16 "ui.chat.attachments.playback_position": "پلے بیک کا مقام" (aria-label of the audio attachment's seek slider, src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/message-item/audio-attachment.tsx:189). This key is the aria-label of the sound player's seek slider (supplement/sound-player.tsx:455) - the same control, two surfaces, two words: a screen-reader user hears مقام on one audio slider and پوزیشن on the other. The style guide asks to "Prefer the settled Urdu term where one exists: ترتیبات (settings), محفوظ کریں (save), استعمال (usage)" and مقام is already the settled word here (64 occurrences in 24 ur files).
findings.recommendation: Use "{label} کا مقام" - note the postposition: مقام is masculine, so کا, not the کی that the feminine پوزیشن selected. That keeps the construction grammatical for any inserted clip title (Urdu marks the genitive on the possessed noun, never on the inserted name) and matches "پلے بیک کا مقام". If the wave prefers the everyday loanword پوزیشن, keep the value and record a follow-up to align ur/ui.chat.attachments.playback_position in a later wave, so the two audio sliders agree on one word.

findings.problem: Observation only, no change requested. ur renders "actions" two ways: اعمال (28 occurrences) and اقدامات (15). The legacy 'actions for {name}' keys use اقدامات - "{name} کے مزید اقدامات" (ui.settings.integrations.json:146) and "{name} فائل کے اقدامات" (ui.projects.json:355) - while the nearest sibling menu uses اعمال: "فائل کے اعمال" (ui.common.actions.json:17). The new keys follow the nearest sibling, which is the correct call for a file/image overflow menu whose unnamed fallback is that same sibling.
findings.recommendation: Keep "{name} کے اعمال" and "تصویر کے اعمال". The اعمال/اقدامات split is pre-existing in namespaces outside this PR; it is recorded here so the ledger note shows it was seen, not missed, and so a later wave can unify the legacy projects/settings keys rather than this PR.

findings.problem: پوزیشن (only occurrence in the ur catalogue) diverges from the settled مقام used for the same audio-seek-slider concept at ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "پلے بیک کا مقام".
findings.recommendation: Prefer "{label} کا مقام" (مقام is masculine: کا); otherwise keep پوزیشن and align the legacy attachments key in a later wave.

findings.problem: Observation only: legacy 'actions for {name}' keys use اقدامات, the nearest sibling menu uses اعمال, and this key follows the sibling.
findings.recommendation: Keep the value; record the pre-existing اعمال/اقدامات split for a later unify wave.

per_key_checks.assessment: Accurate and idiomatic. A short noun phrase for the synthetic filename/caption of an unnamed pasted image; exactly parallels the neighbouring "چسپاں کردہ فائل" (pasted_file) and "چسپاں کردہ {mimeType}" (pasted_type) in construction, register and choice of کردہ over the equally possible کی گئی. کردہ is an invariable perfective participle, so no gender agreement with feminine تصویر is needed or missing. تصویر is already the catalogue's word for image (ui.chat.image_actions.copy_image = "تصویر نقل کریں"). No file extension or MIME prose, per the sidecar note. Sentence case is not applicable to Urdu; no trailing punctuation, matching the English.

placeholder_integrity.note: No placeholder in either language; the note forbids adding one.

per_key_checks.assessment: Grammatical for ANY inserted user string and faithful to the English intent. Urdu marks the genitive on the possessed noun, not on the possessor: کے agrees with اعمال (masculine plural), so the construction is invariant to the name's script, gender, number and trailing punctuation, and no declension can break. It is the catalogue's established idiom for 'actions for X' ("{name} کے مزید اقدامات", "فائل کے اعمال") rather than a literal کے لیے, which would read as 'actions in order that X'. Meaning is not a command to act on the name, and {name} is inserted bare and verbatim with no added extension or quoting. RTL: the leading placeholder is a single LTR island in logical order, which the render layer isolates with FSI/PDI - correct per the style guide's 'do not insert manual bidi control characters', and no such character is present. This is the named-trigger name; the unnamed fallback stays ui.chat.image_actions.actions / file_actions, as the code does (image-actions-menu.tsx:365).

Exact structural parallel to the existing file menu name "فائل کے اعمال" (ui.common.actions.file_actions_menu.file_actions), including the singular noun, which is what English 'Image actions' (not 'images') calls for. Correct for both uses the sidecar names - the menu's default tooltip and the unnamed-image trigger's accessible name - and it correctly stays the generic label while a named image goes through ui.common.actions.actions_for_name. No placeholder, no punctuation, no length hint beyond sanity; 14 characters is compact.

Meaning and grammar are right: پوزیشن is feminine, so کی is the correct postposition (a کا here would have been a grammar error), the phrase names the clip's playback position rather than a play/pause action, and the clip label stays verbatim in front - the same order as the neighbouring "{label} چلائیں" / "{label} کو وقفہ دیں", so a screen reader announces the audio controls consistently. The single reservation is the word itself: پوزیشن is the catalogue's only use of that term, against the settled مقام for the same slider concept (UR-1, MINOR).

context_sidecar_review.pasted_file_broadened_sentence: Verified against source, not assumed. src/renderer/src/features/chat/utils/get-file-name.ts returns t("ui.chat.composer_media.pasted_file") for any non-image data: URI when the name parameter is absent and, through the catch, when decodeURIComponent throws on invalid percent encoding - in both branches regardless of whether a MIME type is present, which is what the sentence now says. src/renderer/src/features/chat/utils/attachment-encode.ts:156-190 confirms the second half: 'Synthetic names for unnamed data URLs ... become upload metadata. Valid decoded names stay verbatim; the original dataUrl (and therefore its bytes/MIME) is passed untouched, and stored metadata wins.' Note for accuracy, not a defect: the composer chip has its own local getFileName (components/attachments-preview.tsx:173-199) which prefers "Pasted {mimeType}" when a MIME type is present, so 'whether or not a MIME type is present' is true of the shared util and of the upload-metadata path it feeds, which is the use the sidecar is describing.
context_sidecar_review.pasted_image_note: Accurate: pasted_image is returned only for a data:image/ URI whose name parameter is absent or fails percent-decoding, and a name that decodes is returned verbatim. It is a display name in attachment rows/captions and in read-failure messages, not a file extension or MIME string.
context_sidecar_review.actions_for_name_note: Accurate: the key is the named file/image trigger's aria-label (supplement-file-actions.tsx:181, image-actions-menu.tsx:365) and both call sites keep the unnamed fallback and caller overrides, as the note states.
context_sidecar_review.position_label_note: Accurate: sound-player.tsx:455 passes the clip label; the string names the seek slider, not play/pause, and does not touch time text or seeking.

rules_applied: No imperatives in any of the four, so the آپ register is untouched; none of them addresses the user.

Settled loanwords in Urdu script are allowed (سیشن، ٹوکن، فائل) - which is why پوزیشن is defensible rather than wrong (UR-1 stays MINOR), and why the guide's 'prefer the settled Urdu term where one exists' line is the reason to prefer مقام.
RTL & bidi: storage logical order, no manual bidi controls, LTR islands byte-identical - all satisfied.
Punctuation: no ۔ ، ؟ ؛ full/half marks appear (no sentence punctuation is needed in any of the four), no Latin punctuation was introduced into prose.
Width: Arabic-script text ~1 cell per character; 14-17 characters, no cap.

typography_and_register.formality: None of the four is an address or an imperative; the polite آپ register is preserved vacuously and nothing colloquial or blunt was introduced.
typography_and_register.register: Short noun phrases, exactly the terse natural Urdu the guide asks for; not Hindi-ised and not over-Persianised (the one Persianate-leaning option, مقام, is already the catalogue's settled word rather than a stylistic import).
typography_and_register.punctuation: No trailing punctuation in any of the four, matching the English; no exclamation mark; no hijacked colon like the ru solution added.
typography_and_register.sentence_case: Not applicable to Urdu script; nothing capitalised or bracketed was introduced.
